source.title: Can Dialects Be Steered Like Languages? Sparse Neurons and Distributed Directions in Arabic LLMs
source.authors: K. Elozeiri; Mervat T. Abassy; Omar Kallas; Fahim Dalvi; Preslav Nakov; Kentaro Inui; Nadir Durrani

record.tranche_reason: The study causally intervenes on selected neurons and compares their effects with unsteered generation and distributed activation-vector steering. This bears conceptually on whether neuron-level units suffice for dialect control, but it does not test the claimed neuron-explanation or attribution-graph methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports no neuron-pole counts for one or two main jobs and does not test explanations on held-out activations. It does test neuron-based dialect steering and residual-subspace coverage, which bear on V5's broader question of whether neuron-level units suffice. Layer and coefficient values used to choose configurations are not recorded as separate result rows. V1–V4 and V6–V7 are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It picks a sparse subset of dialect-selective MLP neurons with the LAPE method and steers generation by rescaling them. It then compares that with residual-stream vector steering and measures how much of the vector direction the selected neurons' output directions span. It never audits what share of neurons have one main job (V1, V2). It does not touch InceptionV1 or recursive generalization (V3), architecture or tool effects (V4), or explanation-to-activation prediction and simulation scoring (V6, V7). For V5, it builds no attribution graph and reports no replacement-model reconstruction error. Its coverage and steering results concern how well a small selected neuron subset (<1% of MLP units) controls dialect. They do not test whether a model's own neurons, as a full basis, suffice as circuit units. This is a steering effect of a selection method, so it belongs under fits_no_version, not V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that dialect information is both sparse and distributed: selected neurons cover only part of the residual direction. Neuron steering can reinforce but not induce dialect, and vector steering is more reliable and the only method that works from MSA prompts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LAPE-selected neuron activation rescaling and residual-stream dialect-minus-MSA vector injection to steer dialect generation. It does not use the original claim's pole-job audit or held-out explanation-scoring procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, dialect, prompt setting, steering layer, coefficient, and number of steered tokens. Neuron amplification settings selected were α = 2.0 for ALLaM and α = 4.0 for Fanar; neuron steering failed on MSA prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: LAPE-selected dialect neurons (<1% of MLP dimensions) span about 5–21% of the residual dialect steering direction. Enrichment over matched random subsets is significant for all Fanar dialects but only some ALLaM dialects. Rescaling these neurons reinforces dialect on dialectal prompts only in some groups and fails entirely on MSA prompts. Residual-vector steering beat neuron steering in 38/40 paired judge tests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A sparse, selectivity-chosen set of individual neurons captures only a minority of a behaviour's residual-stream direction and gives weaker causal control than a distributed direction. This is shown for dialect control in Arabic 7–9B models.

record.problems: The experiments cover only two Arabic-centric models and a limited set of dialects. The paper notes that automatic metrics and the LLM judge do not fully capture output quality, and human annotation exposes a fluency/coherence trade-off for Fanar on Moroccan Arabic. The residual-subspace coverage analysis is not an explanation-prediction test and does not measure attribution-graph reconstruction error.
record.rows_left_out: Not all separately reported vector-steering scores, macro-ADI2 values, vector layer/coefficient/token ablations, reduced-corpus results, or the many other human/LLM metric dimensions are included; these mainly compare vector steering settings or additional metrics beyond the main neuron-sufficiency evidence. See Tables 1–3, 9, 11, and 13 and Figures 3, 5–7, 9–10.

untested.parts: No audit of neuron poles' job shares in Qwen3-32B or any model.
No job-share measurement across models or scale; only two 7–9B Arabic models.
No interpretable-neuron share as a function of architecture, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs from the model's neurons and no replacement-model or reconstruction-error comparison. Only a selected neuron subset is used for steering.
No explanations from activating examples tested for held-out prediction.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked every row to V5 and gave limits_scope and challenges labels. Those links stretch V5, whose claim concerns neuron-based attribution graphs versus trained replacement models, not steering with a selected neuron subset. All verdicts are removed. The study does not cite either original source.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of the share of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or an unknown job.
No such shares are measured across models or scales; only two Arabic-centric models are studied.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or recursive-generalization analysis.
No estimate of interpretable-neuron shares across architectures, tools, or regularization settings.
Tests neuron steering and neuron-subspace coverage for Arabic dialect control, not attribution graphs, general model behavior, or reconstruction error from explanations.
No explanation written from activating examples is tested for predicting firing on new examples.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.operation_detail: Measured residual-subspace coverage of dialect vectors by LAPE-selected MLP-neuron output directions.
rows.value: 12.07% selected-neuron coverage; selected dimension share 0.228%; 804 neurons
rows.note: Coverage is incomplete and the selected set is not significantly enriched over the matched random baseline at the reported empirical p-value.
rows.check: Table 7 residual-subspace coverage measures how much of a dialect steering vector the LAPE-selected subset spans. It does not measure whether neurons as units explain behaviour without a replacement model. Not linked to V5. On its own terms, ALLaM Aleppo, Doha, Rabat and Riyadh (p=0.066–0.388) show no significant enrichment over random subsets, so they are absent relative to that control, not partial.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Mono-dialect prompting across the two models and four evaluated dialect groups
reader_labels.reason: Neuron steering sometimes improved dialect scores but gains were inconsistent across metrics and settings; residual-subspace coverage remained incomplete (r1–r28, r32–r39).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The study reports that neuron steering failed outright in this setting, with minimum dialect-authenticity scores and ADI2 of zero (r29–r30).
